title: Passive 3
subtitle: I was offered ... / I don't like being ... / I was born / get
summary: Use the passive with verbs that have two objects, with -ing forms (being done), with born, and with get in informal English.

lesson.heading: I was offered ... / we were given ...
lesson.text: Some verbs can have two objects. For example, in 'My grandfather gave me this watch', give has two objects: me (object 1) and this watch (object 2). So it is possible to make two passive sentences. Other verbs which can have two objects are **ask, offer, pay, show, tell**.

examples.text: **I was given** this watch (by my grandfather).
This watch **was given to me** (by my grandfather).

lesson.heading: Begin with the person
lesson.text: When we use these verbs in the passive, most often we begin with the person.

examples.text: **I've been offered** the job, but I don't think I want it.
examples.note: = somebody has offered me the job

examples.text: **You will be given** plenty of time to decide.
examples.note: = we will give you plenty of time

examples.text: I didn't see the original document, but **I was shown** a copy.
Tim has an easy job - **he's paid** a lot of money to do very little.

left.label: Active: doing / telling
examples: I don't like people **telling** me what to do.

right.label: Passive: being done / being told
right.text: The passive of doing/seeing etc. is being done / being seen etc.
examples: I don't like **being told** what to do.
I remember **being taken** to the zoo when I was a child. (= I remember somebody taking me to the zoo)
Steve hates **being kept** waiting. (= he hates people keeping him waiting)
We climbed over the wall without **being seen**. (= without anybody seeing us)

lesson.heading: I was born ...
lesson.text: We say 'I **was born** ...' (not I am born) when we talk about a person's birth in the past. The present form (are born) is only for general facts about births happening now.

examples.text: How many babies **are born** every day?

lesson.heading: get
lesson.text: You can use **get** for the passive. We use get only when things happen, and mainly in informal spoken English. You can use be in all situations.

examples.text: There was a fight, but nobody **got hurt**.
I don't **get invited** to many parties.
I'm surprised Liz didn't **get offered** the job.
Peter was a mystery man. Very little **was known** about him.

lesson.text: With give, offer, pay, show, tell and ask, start the passive sentence with the person: I was given / I was told / I was asked.

exercises.prompt: My grandfather gave me this watch. Which passive sentence has the same meaning?
options: I was given this watch by my grandfather.
This watch gave me by my grandfather.
I am given this watch by my grandfather.
exercises.explanation: Give has two objects, and we usually begin the passive with the person: I was given this watch.

exercises.prompt: Amy retired from her job recently. She ___ a present by her colleagues.
exercises.explanation: Begin with the person: she was given a present (= her colleagues gave her a present).

exercises.prompt: Complete each sentence with the correct ending using being + verb.

pairs.left: We went to the wedding without
It's a busy road and I don't like crossing it. I'm afraid of
I'm an adult. I don't like

pairs.right: being stuck in a traffic jam.

exercises.prompt: You will need to use this machine. Have you ___ how it works?
exercises.explanation: Present perfect passive beginning with the person: Have you been shown ...? (= has somebody shown you?)
Where were you born? A person's birth is in the past, so we say was/were born.

exercises.prompt: Alex ___ by a bee while he was sitting in the garden.
exercises.explanation: Something happened to Alex, so get is possible for the passive: got stung (= was stung).

exercises.prompt: She's a voluntary worker. She ___ get paid.
exercises.explanation: Get is an ordinary verb here, so the negative is doesn't get paid (= she isn't paid).

exercises.prompt: I was surprised to get the job I applied for. I didn't expect ___ it.
exercises.explanation: Passive infinitive after expect: to be offered (= I didn't expect somebody to offer me the job).

exercises.prompt: Make the passive sentence that begins with the watch. (this watch / give / me / my grandfather)
exercises.answer: This watch was given to me by my grandfather.
exercises.explanation: When the thing is the subject, we need to before the person: was given to me.
Jessica is liked by everybody. We use get only when things happen - being liked is not a 'happening'.

exercises.prompt: These tennis courts don't ___ very often. Not many people want to play here.
exercises.explanation: Get + past participle for something that happens: don't get used (= aren't used).

exercises.statement: I remember being taken to the zoo when I was a child.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Being taken is the passive -ing form (= I remember somebody taking me to the zoo).
